Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). Al-Nasa'i related from al-Bara', who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter." It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave: it is said to him, "Who is your Lord?" and he says, "My Lord is Allah, and my religion is the religion of Muhammad." That is His saying: "Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter."

I say: This has also come in this form as a mawquf report (ending with al-Bara') in some chains of Muslim from al-Bara' [that] it is his saying [[i.e., the saying of al-Bara'.]]. The sound version of it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet), as in the Sahih of Muslim and the books of al-Nasa'i, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah and others, from al-Bara' from the Prophet ﷺ [[In some manuscripts: "Al-Bara' said."]]. Al-Bukhari mentioned: Ja'far ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When the believer is seated in his grave, a visitor comes to him, then he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. That is His saying: 'Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.'" We have explained this topic in the book "al-Tadhkirah," and we have explained there who is tested in his grave and questioned, so whoever wishes to examine it should consult it there.

Sahl ibn ʿAmmar said: I saw Yazid ibn Harun in a dream after his death, and I said to him: "What did Allah do with you?" He said: "Two angels, harsh and severe, came to me in my grave and said: 'What is your religion, who is your Lord, and who is your Prophet?' So I seized my white beard and said: 'Is such a question put to someone like me, when I have taught people your answer for eighty years?!' So they left and said [[In al-Tahdhib there is something other than this, so it should be consulted.]]: 'Did you write from Harir ibn ʿUthman?' I said: 'Yes!' They said: 'Indeed he used to hate [ʿAli] [[In the originals it reads "Uthman," and likewise in the author's "al-Tadhkirah." What is in "Tahdhib al-Tahdhib" is that he used to hate ʿAli.]], so Allah hated him.'"

It was also said: the meaning of "Allah keeps firm" is that Allah keeps them constant upon the firm word. From this is the saying of ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah:

May Allah keep firm what He has given you of good, a firmness like that of Moses, and a victory like the one that was granted (to him).

It was also said: He keeps them firm in both abodes as a recompense for them for the firm word. Al-Qaffal and a group said: "In the life of this world" means in the grave, because the dead are in the world until they are resurrected; "and in the Hereafter" means at the reckoning. Al-Mawardi related it from al-Bara', who said: "The life of this world" refers to the questioning in the grave, and "the Hereafter" to the questioning on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And Allah leads astray the wrongdoers﴾, meaning from their proof in their graves, just as they went astray in this world through their disbelief, so He does not make them hear the word of truth. When they are questioned in their graves they say: "We do not know," and it is said to them: "You did not know, and you did not recite" [[It has been said regarding "wa la tulita": "wa la tulawta," meaning "nor did you recite," from talā yatlū; they said "tuliyta" with a yā' so that it would substitute for the yā' in "daryta."]], and at that point they are struck with maqami' [[The maqami': whips of iron with curved heads.]], as is established in the reports, and we have mentioned that in the book "al-Tadhkirah." It was also said: He gives them respite until they increase in error in this world.

﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾ regarding the punishment of one people and the misguidance of another. It was also said: the occasion of revelation of this verse is what is related from the Prophet ﷺ: when he described the questioning by Munkar and Nakir and what the dead person's answer would be, ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, will my intellect be with me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am sufficient," and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 28–30:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude (kufr)﴾. That is, they made disbelief (kufr) a substitute for the favor of Allah upon them, in their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ), when Allah sent him to them, from among them and in their midst, so they disbelieved. The intended ones are the polytheists of Quraysh, and the verse was revealed concerning them, related from Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAli and others. It was also said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists who fought the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Badr. Abu al-Tufayl said: I heard ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "They are the Quraysh who were slaughtered on the day of Badr." It was also said: it was revealed concerning the two most wicked clans of Quraysh, Banu Makhzum and Banu Umayya. As for Banu Umayya, they were allowed to enjoy (their lives) for a time, and as for Banu Makhzum, they were destroyed on the day of Badr. This was said by ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both. A fourth opinion: they are Jabalah ibn al-Ayham, the chief of the Arab Christians (mutanassirah), and his companions, when he was slapped and ʿUmar gave him the right of retaliation with the same (slap). He was not content and was too proud, so he apostatized, became a Christian, and joined the Romans with a group of his people. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah. When he reached the land of the Romans he regretted it and said:

The nobles became Christian out of the shame of a slap,
and there was no harm in it had you been patient with it.
Stubbornness and pride held me back from it,
and I sold for it my sound eye for a blind one.
So would that I were herding camels in some land,
and had not denied the saying that ʿUmar said.

Al-Hasan said: it is general to all polytheists.

(And they caused their people to alight) meaning, they made them descend. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr. "They caused their people to alight," meaning those who followed them.

(into the abode of ruin) It was said: Hell, related by Ibn Zayd. It was also said: the day of Badr, related by ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and Mujahid. Al-Bawar means destruction, and from it is the saying of the poet:

I have not seen their like as champions of war,
on the morning of battle, when ruin was feared.

(Hell, which they will enter) It clarifies that the abode of ruin is Hell, as Ibn Zayd said. According to this, it is not permissible to pause at "abode of ruin," because Jahannam is in the accusative as an apposition (tarjamah) to "abode of ruin." But if someone were to raise it by an implied subject, meaning "it is Jahannam," or by the pronoun returning in "they will enter it," the pause at "abode of ruin" would be acceptable.

(And wretched is the settling place) meaning the place of residence.

His saying, Exalted is He: (And they set up rivals to Allah) meaning idols they worshipped, and this has already been discussed in al-Baqarah.[[See vol. 1, p. 230 onward.]]

(to lead astray from His way) meaning from His religion. Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read with a fatha on the yāʾ (liyuḍilla), and likewise in al-Hajj: ﴿liyuḍilla ʿan sabīlillāh﴾ [al-Hajj: 9], and similarly in Luqman and al-Zumar.[[See vol. 12, p. 16, and vol. 15, p. 237.]] The rest read it with a ḍammah (liyuḍillū), meaning "that they may lead people astray from His way." As for the one who reads with a fatha, the meaning is that they themselves go astray from the way of Allah continually, i.e., their outcome is misguidance and going astray; this is the lam of consequence (lam al-ʿāqibah).

(Say: enjoy yourselves) a warning to them, and it indicates the diminishing of what they have of the worldly pleasures, since it is cut off.

(for indeed your destiny is the Fire) meaning your return and your place of return is the punishment of Hell.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed﴾, meaning: the people of Makkah have exchanged the blessing of Allah for disbelief, so say to those who have believed and fulfilled their servitude to Him that they should ﴿establish the prayer﴾, meaning the five daily prayers. That is, say to them, "Establish." The imperative here carries an implied condition, as when you say, "Obey Allah and He will admit you into Paradise," meaning: if you obey Him, He will admit you into Paradise. This is the view of al-Farra'. Al-Zajjaj said: "yuqimu" (they should establish) is in the jussive mood with the sense of the lam (of command), meaning "li-yuqimu" (so that they may establish), and the lam was dropped because the imperative "qul" (say) indicates the absent third person. He said: It is also possible to say that "yuqimu" is the answer to an omitted imperative, meaning: say to them, "Establish the prayer," and they will establish the prayer.

﴿And spend of what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾, meaning the zakah, according to Ibn 'Abbas and others. The majority said: the secret is what is hidden and the open is what is apparent. Al-Qasim ibn Yahya said: the secret is voluntary charity and the open is obligatory charity. This meaning has already been discussed in detail in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 3, pp. 332 onward and p. 266 onward.]] at His saying: ﴿If you give charity openly, it is good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 271].

﴿Before there comes a Day in which there is no trade nor friendship﴾. This has also been discussed earlier in al-Baqarah [[See vol. 3, pp. 332 onward and p. 266 onward.]]. "Khilal" is the plural of "khullah," like "qullah" and "qilal." [[Said by Imru' al-Qays, and the first half of the verse is: "Sarafa al-hawa 'anhunna min khashyati al-radda."]] He said: "So you are not one who is weary of friendship, nor one who hates."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 32–34:

Allah's saying: ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning He originated and invented them without any prior pattern.

(And sent down from the sky) meaning from the clouds.

(water, and brought forth thereby fruits) meaning fruits from the trees, (as provision for you).

(And subjected to you the ship, that it may sail through the sea by His command) Its meaning has already been mentioned in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 2, p. 194.]].

(And subjected to you the rivers) meaning the sweet seas, so that you may drink from them, water your animals and cultivate, and the salty seas for the varied benefits from their sides.

(And subjected to you the sun and the moon, both continuing [in their courses]) meaning, in bringing about what they bring about of plants and other things. Ad-du'ub (continuity) is the passing of a thing through its work in a customary, ongoing manner. It was said: "continuing in motion" in obedience to Allah's command, and the meaning is that they keep running until the Day of Resurrection without slackening. This meaning was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

(And subjected to you the night and the day) meaning so that you may rest at night and seek His bounty during the day, as He said: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [[See vol. 13, p. 108.]] [al-Qasas: 73].

Allah's saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾, meaning He gave you of every thing you asked Him for something, with the object omitted, according to al-Akhfash. It was also said: the meaning is "and He gave you of all that you asked Him for and of all that you did not ask Him for," with the latter part omitted; so we did not ask Him for the sun, the moon, or many of His blessings with which He began us. This is like His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [[See vol. 10, p. 160.]] [an-Nahl: 81], as will come. It was also said: "min" is extra, meaning He gave you everything you asked Him for. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and others read "wa-atakum min kullin" with tanwin, "ma sa'altumuhu". This reading has also been narrated from al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatadah; it is in the sense of negation, meaning "of every thing you did not ask Him for," such as the sun, the moon and others. It was also said: "of every thing that you asked Him for," meaning "that which you did not ask Him for."

(And if you should count the favour of Allah) meaning the favours of Allah.

(you could not enumerate them) and you would not be able to count them or confine them, due to their abundance, such as hearing and sight, the forming of figures, and other things such as well-being and provision. [Blessings that cannot be counted.] [[From the manuscript margins.]] These blessings are from Allah, so why do you exchange the blessing of Allah for disbelief? And why do you not seek help through them in obedience?! (Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer, a great ingrate) "Al-insan" is a generic noun, and by it is meant a specific group. Ibn 'Abbas said: he meant Abu Jahl. It was also said: all disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 35–36:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾ — meaning Makkah. It has already been discussed in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 2, p. 117 onward.]].

(And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols) — i.e., make me distant from their worship. By his saying "keep me away" he meant his sons from his own loins, and they were eight, and none of them worshipped an idol. It was also said: it is a supplication on behalf of whoever Allah willed that he should supplicate for. Al-Jahdari and Isa read "wa-ajnibni" with an alif at the beginning, and the meaning is one: it is said, "janabtu dhalika al-amr," "ajnabtuhu," and "jannabtuhu iyyahu," so he kept away from it (tajannabahu) and avoided it (ijtanabahu), i.e., left it. Ibrahim al-Taymi used to say in his storytelling: "Who can feel safe from trial after the Friend (Khalil) when he says, 'And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols,' just as my father and my people worshipped them?"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ — since they were a cause of misguidance, he attributed the act to them figuratively, for idols are inanimate objects that do not act [[Fa-y-a: lā taʿqil (do not reason).]].

(So whoever follows me) in monotheism,

(then indeed he is of me) i.e., of the people of my religion.

(And whoever disobeys me) i.e., persists in polytheism,

(then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful). It was said: he said this before Allah informed him that Allah does not forgive that He be associated with. It was also said: "Forgiving and Merciful" toward whoever repents of his sin before death. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "And whoever disobeys me" refers to what is less than polytheism.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 35–36:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾ — meaning Makkah. It has already been discussed in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 2, p. 117 onward.]].

(And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols) — i.e., make me distant from their worship. By his saying "keep me away" he meant his sons from his own loins, and they were eight, and none of them worshipped an idol. It was also said: it is a supplication on behalf of whoever Allah willed that he should supplicate for. Al-Jahdari and Isa read "wa-ajnibni" with an alif at the beginning, and the meaning is one: it is said, "janabtu dhalika al-amr," "ajnabtuhu," and "jannabtuhu iyyahu," so he kept away from it (tajannabahu) and avoided it (ijtanabahu), i.e., left it. Ibrahim al-Taymi used to say in his storytelling: "Who can feel safe from trial after the Friend (Khalil) when he says, 'And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols,' just as my father and my people worshipped them?"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ — since they were a cause of misguidance, he attributed the act to them figuratively, for idols are inanimate objects that do not act [[Fa-y-a: lā taʿqil (do not reason).]].

(So whoever follows me) in monotheism,

(then indeed he is of me) i.e., of the people of my religion.

(And whoever disobeys me) i.e., persists in polytheism,

(then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful). It was said: he said this before Allah informed him that Allah does not forgive that He be associated with. It was also said: "Forgiving and Merciful" toward whoever repents of his sin before death. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "And whoever disobeys me" refers to what is less than polytheism.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 37 (part 1 of 2):**

There are six issues in this verse.

**The first issue:** Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The first time women used the *mintaq* [[al-mintaq: the *nitaq*, which is when a woman puts on her garment, then ties something around her waist and raises the middle of her garment and lets it hang down below, when doing work, so that she does not trip over its hem]] was from the mother of Isma'il. She made a *mintaq* so that she could conceal her trail from Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Isma'il while she was nursing him, until he placed them by the House, beside a tree above Zamzam, at the top of the mosque. There was no one in Makkah at that time, and there was no water there. He placed them there and placed beside them a leather bag containing dates and a waterskin containing water. Then Ibrahim turned to leave, and the mother of Isma'il followed him and said: 'O Ibrahim! Where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person [[In manuscripts ى and و: *anis*.]] and nothing?' She said this to him many times, but he did not turn towards her. So she said to him: 'Has Allah commanded you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not neglect us.' She then went back, and Ibrahim left. When he reached the *Thaniyya*, where they could not see him, he faced the House and made these supplications, raising his hands, and said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation﴾ [Ibrahim: 37], until he reached 'they may give thanks.' The mother of Isma'il kept nursing Isma'il and drinking from that water, until the water in the waterskin ran out. She became thirsty and her son became thirsty too, and she began to watch him writhing, or he said *yatalabbat* [[*yatalabbat*: rolling in the dust.]], so she set off, out of distress at looking at him. She found al-Safa to be the nearest mountain to her in the land, so she stood upon it, then faced the valley, looking to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She descended from al-Safa, and when she reached the valley she lifted the edge of her garment and then ran with the effort of a person in distress, until she crossed the valley. Then she came to al-Marwa and stood upon it, looking to see whether she could see anyone, but she saw no one. She did this seven times." Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "That is the running [*sa'y*] of people between them." When she came near al-Marwa she heard a voice and said: '*Sah!*' [[*Sah*: a word used to silence someone, meaning 'be quiet', here addressed to herself.]] meaning herself. Then she listened attentively and heard it again, and said: 'You have made me hear, so if you have help [*ghawath*] [[*Ghawath* (with a fatha): like *ghiyath* (with a kasra), from *al-ighatha*, which means assistance.]] then help me!' Suddenly she saw the angel at the place of Zamzam, and he scraped with his heel [or he said: with his wing] until the water appeared. She began to make a basin for it [*tuhawwiduh*] and said [[*Wa-taqulu*: "and she says with her hand like this." This is a report of her action, and it is one of the cases where speech is used for action.]] with her hand, like this, and she began to scoop water into her waterskin, and the water kept gushing up after she scooped it. Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. If she had left Zamzam alone, or he said: if she had not scooped from the water, Zamzam would have become a flowing spring." He said: "So she drank and nursed her child, and the angel said to her: 'Do not fear abandonment, for here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build, and Allah does not neglect His people.'" He mentioned the hadith in full.

**Issue:** No one may use this story as a basis for abandoning his child and dependents in a barren land, relying on the Almighty, the Merciful, and imitating the act of Ibrahim the Friend of Allah, as the extremist Sufis say concerning the reality of *tawakkul* [[*Tawakkul*: complete reliance upon Allah.]]. Ibrahim did this by the command of Allah, as shown by his words in the hadith: "Has Allah commanded you to do this?" He said: "Yes." It has also been narrated that when Sarah became jealous of Hajar after she had borne Isma'il, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, took her out to Makkah. It is related that he rode the *Buraq* with Hajar and the infant, and in a single day he came from al-Sham to the valley of Makkah. He left his son and his maidservant there and rode back the same day. All of this was by revelation from Allah, the Exalted. When he turned to leave, he made supplication, which is contained in the meaning of this verse.

**The second issue:** When Allah willed to establish this situation, prepare the station, and mark out the place for the Sacred House and the Sacred City, He sent the angel, who scraped for water and made it a substitute for food. It is recorded in the authentic collection that Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, sustained himself on it for thirty days and nights. Abu Dhar said: "I had no food except the water of Zamzam, and I grew so fat that my skin folds [*'ukan*] [[*'Ukan*: plural of *'ukna*, which is the flesh of the belly that folds and creases through fatness.]] became creased, and I did not feel any weakness [*sakhfa*] [[*Sakhfat al-jû'*: its thinness and weakness.]] of hunger in my liver," and he mentioned the hadith.

Al-Daraqutni narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for. If you drink it seeking healing, Allah will heal you. If you drink it to satisfy your hunger, Allah will satisfy you with it. If you drink it to quench your thirst, it will quench it. It is the *hazma* [[*Hazmat Jibril*: that is, he struck it with his foot, and the water gushed forth.]] of Jibril and the watering of Allah for Isma'il."

It is also narrated from 'Ikrima, who said: Whenever Ibn 'Abbas drank from Zamzam, he would say: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every disease."

Ibn al-'Arabi said: This benefit remains in it until the Day of Resurrection for whoever has sound intention, a pure heart, does not deny it, and does not drink it as a mere test. For Allah is with those who rely upon Him, and He exposes those who test Him.

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, told me: "I entered the *tawaf* on a dark night, and I was overcome by the need to urinate, which preoccupied me. I kept holding it in [*a'tasir*] [[*Al-'asr*: restraint and confinement.]] until it pained me. I feared that if I left the mosque I would step on some of those feet, and it was the days of the Hajj. So I recalled this hadith, entered Zamzam, and drank from it until I was satisfied [*tadallu'tu*], and the need left me until morning."

It is also narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: "Indeed, in Zamzam there is a spring from Paradise, from the direction of the Corner [*al-Rukn*]."

**The third issue:** Allah's words ﴿from my offspring﴾: the word "from" [*min*] in His words "from my offspring" indicates partitive meaning, meaning: I have settled *some* of my offspring, namely Isma'il and his mother, because Ishaq was in al-Sham. It has also been said that the "from" is redundant [*silah*], meaning: I have settled my offspring.

**The fourth issue:** Allah's words ﴿near Your Sacred House﴾ indicate that the House was ancient, according to what has been narrated, existing before the Flood. This meaning has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqara [[See vol. 2, p. 120 onward.]]. He attributed the House to Himself because no one else owns it, and He described it as "sacred" [*muharram*], meaning that what is permitted elsewhere, such as sexual intercourse and violation, is forbidden in it. It has also been said that it is forbidden to tyrants, and that its sanctity should not be violated or its rights treated lightly. This was said by Qatada and others. This matter has already been discussed in Surat al-Ma'ida [[See vol. 6, p. 325.]].

**The fifth issue:** Allah's words ﴿Our Lord, that they may establish the prayer﴾: He singled it out from among the whole of the religion because of its excellence and its station within it. It is the covenant of Allah with His servants. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Five prayers which Allah has prescribed for the servants," and he mentioned the hadith.

The *lam* in "that they may establish the prayer" is the *lam* of purpose [*lam kay*]. This is the apparent reading, and it is connected to "I have settled." It is also possible that it is the *lam* of command [*lam amr*], as if he was asking Allah [to entrust them to Him] [[In manuscript ى: *an ya'tamanahum*.]] and to grant them success in establishing the prayer.

**The sixth issue:** This verse contains the indication that prayer in Makkah is more excellent than prayer elsewhere, because the meaning of "Our Lord, that they may establish the prayer" is: I have settled them by Your Sacred House so that they may establish the prayer in it. The scholars have differed over whether prayer in Makkah is more excellent or prayer in the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. The majority of the people of narration [*Ahl al-Athar*] [[*Ahl al-Athar*: the scholars who rely on transmitted reports.]] held that prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is more excellent than prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ. The hadith: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-Masjid al-Haram, and a prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than a prayer in this mosque of mine by a hundred prayers."

The Imam and memorizer Abu 'Umar said: Habib al-Mu'allim transmitted this hadith with a chain going back to 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and he made it sound, without confusing its wording or meaning. He was trustworthy. Ibn Abi Khaythama said: I heard Yahya ibn Ma'in say: "Habib al-Mu'allim is trustworthy." 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad mentioned: I heard my father say: "Habib al-Mu'allim is trustworthy, how sound his hadith is!" Abu Zur'a al-Razi was asked about Habib al-Mu'allim and said: "He is a trustworthy Basran."

I say: Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Tamimi al-Busti has also recorded this hadith of Habib al-Mu'allim from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from the Prophet ﷺ, in his *al-Musnad al-Sahih*. Therefore the hadith is sound, and it is the proof when there is dispute and disagreement. All praise is due to Allah.

Abu 'Umar said: It has also been narrated from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, a report similar to the hadith of Ibn al-Zubayr, transmitted by Musa al-Juhani from Nafi', from Ibn 'Amr. Musa al-Juhani [al-Kufi] [[From manuscript ى: he is Musa ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani al-Kufi.]] is trustworthy; al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya, and a group of them praised him. Shu'ba, al-Thawri, and Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated from him. Hakim ibn Sayf narrated: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar told us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other, except al-Masjid al-Haram. A prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than a hundred thousand prayers elsewhere."

This Hakim ibn Sayf is a shaykh from the people of al-Raqqa. Abu Zur'a al-Razi narrated from him, and Ibn Wadhdhah took from him. In their view he is a truthful shaykh with nothing wrong with him. If he memorized it, then there are two hadiths [in these two narrations]; otherwise, the word is that of Habib al-Mu'allim.

Muhammad ibn Wadhdhah narrated: Yusuf ibn 'Adi told us, from 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-Masjid al-Haram, for prayer in it is better."

Abu 'Umar said: All of this is explicit text on the point of disagreement, decisive for whoever has been granted right guidance and whose partisanship does not incline him away from it. Ibn Habib reported from Mutarrif and from Asbagh, from Ibn Wahb, that both of them held the view that prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is superior to prayer in the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ, on the basis of what is in this chapter.

Malik and all the other scholars agreed that the two festival prayers are performed in open ground [*yabruz lahuma*] in every town, except Makkah, where they are performed in al-Masjid al-Haram. 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu al-Darda', and Jabir preferred Makkah and its mosque. They are more worthy of being followed than those who came after them. This is also the view of al-Shafi'i, and it is the view of 'Ata' and the scholars of Makkah and Kufa. A similar view is also reported from Malik. Ibn Wahb mentioned in his *Jami'* from Malik that when Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down to the earth, he said: "O Lord, is this the one most beloved to You that You be worshipped in it?" He said: "No, rather Makkah." What is well known from Malik and the people of Madina is the preference of Madina. The people of Basra and Baghdad differed on this: one group says Makkah, and another group says Madina.

**Allah's words:** ﴿So make hearts from among the people incline towards them﴾. *Af'ida* is the plural of *fu'ad*, which means hearts. The heart is sometimes expressed by *fu'ad*, as the poet said:

*And indeed a heart that led me with passion*
*towards you, despite the long passage of time, is patient.*

"It is also said: it is the plural of wafd (delegation), and the original was awfidah; the fa' was moved forward and the waw changed to ya' as it stands, so it is as if he said: 'Make a company (wufud) of people incline towards them,' i.e. yearn for them. It is said: hawiya nahwahu (he inclined toward it) when he leaned toward it, and the she-camel hawat tahwi hawiyan, so she is hawiyah, when she ran a severe run, as if she were in the depth of a well. His saying 'tahwi ilayhim' (yearns toward them) is derived from this. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: 'Had he said "af'idatan-nas" (hearts of people), Persia, the Romans, the Turks, the Indians, the Jews, the Christians and the Magians would have crowded upon it. But he said "min an-nas" (from the people), and they are the Muslims. So His saying "tahwi ilayhim" means: yearn toward them, and long to visit the House.' Mujahid recited "tahwahum" (tahwi ilayhim) meaning: love them and honour them.[[Al-Alusi said: the present tense of hawa in the sense of "love," which takes ila.]]

(And provide for them with fruits, that they may give thanks.) So Allah answered his supplication, and caused all kinds of trees to grow for them at al-Ta'if, and [provided] what is brought to them from the cities.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas, is the long hadith, of which we have mentioned part: "Ibrahim came after Isma'il had married, to check on his property, but did not find Isma'il. He asked his wife about him, and she said: 'He has gone out seeking provision for us.' Then he asked them about their livelihood and their condition, and she said: 'We are in a bad state; we are in hardship and distress,' and she complained to him. He said: 'When your husband comes, convey my greetings to him and tell him to change the threshold of his door.' When Isma'il came, he seemed to sense something [[i.e., he saw and perceived something he was not accustomed to.]] and said: 'Has anyone come to you?' She said: 'Yes, an old man of such and such description came to us, and he asked about you, and I informed him, and he asked me about our living, and I told him that we are in hardship and distress.' He said: 'Did he enjoin anything upon you?' She said: 'He commanded me to convey his greetings to you, and he says: change the threshold of your door.' He said: 'That was my father, and he has commanded me to part from you; go back to your family.' So he divorced her and married another woman from them. Ibrahim stayed away from them as long as Allah willed, then came to them again, but did not find him, and entered upon his wife and asked her about him. She said: 'He has gone out seeking provision for us.' He said: 'How are you?' and asked her about their living and condition. She said: 'We are in good condition and plenty,' and she praised Allah. He said: 'What is your food?' She said: 'Meat.' He said: 'What is your drink?' She said: 'Water.' He said: 'O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'At that time they had no grain; had they had it, he would have prayed for them in it.' He said: 'Neither of the two of them is entered upon by anyone without their land being unsuitable for him except that they do not agree with him,' and he mentioned the hadith."

And Ibn 'Abbas said: His saying "So make hearts of people incline towards them" (Ibrahim) asked that Allah make people desire to dwell in Makkah, so that it would become a sacred house. All of that came about, and praise be to Allah. The first to settle it were the Jurhum.

In al-Bukhari, after his saying: "Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of those who are its people," [the hadith continues]: "The House was raised up from the ground like a mound; the torrents came to it and took away from its right and its left. Thus it was until a caravan of Jurhum passed by them, returning from the road of such-and-such, and they camped at the lower part of Makkah. They saw a bird circling (a 'ā'if, one that hovers over water and does not depart), and they said: 'This bird is surely circling around water! We know this valley, and there is no water in it.' So they sent one or two messengers [[al-jari: the messenger.]], and they found water, and informed them of the water, and they came. He said: Umm Isma'il was by the water, and they said: 'Will you permit us to stay with you?' She said: 'Yes, but you have no right to the water.' They said: 'Yes.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "[Then he found] (Umm Isma'il found that Jurhumi clan, or the request of Jurhum to dwell found Umm Isma'il, while she loved companionship; so the subject of 'found' is 'that,' and 'that' refers to the request for permission) that, Umm Isma'il, and she loved companionship." So they settled and sent for their families, and they settled with them, until there were households among them there. The boy grew up, and Umm Isma'il died. Then Ibrahim came after Isma'il had married, to check on his property... the hadith.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran, "The Compendium of the Rulings of the Quran") on surah 14, verses 38–41:**

The words of God, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare﴾. That is, nothing of our circumstances is hidden from You. Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: "You know all that I conceal and all that I declare, of the grief over Isma'il and his mother, when they were settled in a valley without crops."

(﴿And nothing is hidden from God, on earth or in heaven﴾). It has been said that this is from the words of Ibrahim. It has also been said that it is from the words of God, the Exalted: when Ibrahim said, "Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare," God said, "And nothing is hidden from God, on earth or in heaven."

(﴿All praise is due to God, who has granted me, in old age, [Isma'il and Ishaq]﴾). That is, in my old age and the old age of my wife. Ibn 'Abbas said: Isma'il was born to him when he was ninety-nine years old, and Ishaq when he was one hundred and twelve years old. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibrahim was given the good news of Ishaq after a hundred and ten years.

(﴿Indeed my Lord is All-Hearing of supplication﴾). The words of God, the Exalted: ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer﴾, that is, among those who remain firm upon Islam and adhere to its rulings.

(﴿And from my descendants﴾), that is, and make among my descendants those who establish it.

(﴿Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾), that is, my worship. As He says: ﴿And your Lord says: "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. [See vol. 15, p. 326.] The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Supplication is the essence of worship." This has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah. [See vol. 2, p. 309 and following.]

(﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers﴾). It has been said that Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his parents before it became clear to him that they were enemies of God. Al-Qushayri said: It is not far-fetched that his mother was a Muslim, because God mentioned his excuse for asking forgiveness for his father but not for his mother. I say: On this basis is the reading of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, "My Lord, forgive me and my parents," meaning his father. It has also been said that he asked forgiveness for them out of hope for their faith. It has been said that he asked forgiveness for them on the condition that they embrace Islam. It has also been said that he meant Adam and Eve. It has been narrated that when a servant says, "O God, forgive me and my parents," and his parents had died as disbelievers, the forgiveness is directed to Adam and Eve, since they are the parents of all creation. It has also been said that he meant his two sons, Isma'il and Ishaq. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to recite "and for my sons" (wa-li-waladayya), meaning his two sons, and Yahya ibn Ya'mar also recited it thus. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi and al-Nahhas.

(﴿And for the believers﴾). Ibn 'Abbas said: from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). It has also been said: "for the believers" in general, and this is the more apparent view.

(﴿On the Day when the Reckoning is established﴾), that is, the Day when people stand for the reckoning.

**The Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 14, verses 42–43:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾. This is a consolation (tasliyah) for the Prophet ﷺ after the actions of the polytheists and their opposition to the religion of Ibrahim had troubled him. The meaning is: be patient as Ibrahim was patient, and inform the polytheists that the delay of the punishment does not mean He approves of their deeds, but rather it is the way of Allah to give rebellious people respite for a period. Maymun ibn Mihran said: "This is a warning to the wrongdoer and a consolation to the wronged."

(﴿He only defers them﴾) meaning the polytheists of Makkah: He gives them respite and delays their punishment. The common reading (qira'ah) is "yu'akhkhiruhum" with the letter ya', and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it because of His saying: "And do not think that Allah". It was read by al-Hasan and al-Sulami, and it is also reported from Abu 'Amr, as "nu'akhkhiruhum" with the letter nun, for magnification.

(﴿for a Day when eyes will stare fixed﴾) meaning, they will not close their eyes because of the terror of what they see on that Day. This was said by al-Farra'. It is said: "shakhasa al-rajul basarahu" (the man fixed his gaze), and "shakhasa al-basar" means the sight itself rose and lifted up because of the terror of what it sees. Ibn 'Abbas said: The eyes of all creatures will be fixed on that Day upon the sky, out of extreme bewilderment, so they will not blink.

(﴿hastening﴾, muhti'in) meaning hurrying. This was said by al-Hasan, Qatadah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It is derived from "ahta'a yuhti'u ihta'an" when one hastens, and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿hastening toward the caller﴾ [al-Qamar: 8], meaning hurrying. The poet said:

*In Dijlah is their dwelling, and indeed I see them*
*In Dijlah, hastening toward the sound of the summons.*

It was also said: "al-muhti'" is one who looks in humiliation and humbleness, that is, gazing without blinking. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: "muhti'in" means those who keep their gaze constant. Al-Nahhas said: "The known usage in the language is to say 'ahta'a' when one hastens." Abu 'Ubayd said: "Both meanings may be intended together, that is, hastening with a constant gaze." Ibn Zayd said: "The muhti' is one who does not raise his head."

(﴿with heads raised﴾, muqni'i ru'usihim) meaning, lifting their heads, looking in humiliation. Iqna' al-ra's means raising it, as said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid. Ibn 'Arafah, al-Qutabi and others said: "The muqni' is one who raises his head and directs his gaze at what is before him." From this is "al-iqna' fi al-salah" [Iqna' in prayer means that the one praying raises his head until it is higher than his back], and "aqna'a sawtahu" when he raises his voice. Al-Hasan said: "The faces of people on that Day will be toward the sky; no one will look at anyone else." It was also said: "lowering their heads." Al-Mahdawi said: "It is said 'aqna'a' when he raised his head, and 'aqna'a' when he lowered his head in humiliation and submission. The verse admits both meanings, and this was said by al-Mubarrad. But the first opinion is better known in the language." The rajaz poet said:

*He shook his head toward me and raised it [aqna'a],*
*As if he had seen something that made him covet.*

Al-Shammakh said, describing camels:

*They come early to the acacia trees with raised heads [bi-muqni'at],*
*Their molars like sharp hatchets.*

He means: with heads raised toward them so that they may reach them. From this, a woman's head-covering is called "muqana'ah" because of its height. From this, "qana'a al-rajul" means he was content, that is, he raised his head from asking. "Qana'a" also means he asked, that is, he came to what one would be ashamed of, from al-Nahhas. "Fam muqna'" means a mouth whose teeth are bent inward. "Rajul muqannaf" with a shadda means he wears a helmet, as said by al-Jawhari.

(﴿their gaze will not return to them﴾) meaning, their eyes will not return to them from the intensity of looking, so their gaze remains fixed. It is said: "taraf al-rajul yatrif tarfan" when he closes one eyelid over the other, and gaze is called "tarf" because it occurs through it. "Al-tarf" also means the eye. 'Antarah said:

*I lower my gaze whenever my neighbour appears to me,*
*Until she is hidden in her dwelling.*

Jamil said:

*I restrain my gaze out of honour for Jumal,*
*For Jumal, and for the gaze that I restrain.*

(﴿and their hearts are hawa'﴾) meaning, they are not benefited by anything because of the intensity of fear. Ibn 'Abbas: empty of all good. Al-Suddi: their hearts came out of their chests and lodged in their throats. Mujahid, Murrah and Ibn Zayd said: hollow, ruined, torn apart [in W: "burnt"], with nothing good or reason in them, like your saying about a house in which there is nothing: "it is only empty air." This was also said by Ibn 'Abbas. In the language, "hawa'" is what is hollow and empty. From this is the saying of Hassan:

*Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me:*
*You are a hollow, heartless coward.*

Zuhayr said, describing a camel with a small head:

*As if the rider upon her, above a small-headed one [sa'l],*
*Of the ostriches, his breast is empty air.*

"Fari'" means empty, that is, void. In the revelation: ﴿And the heart of Musa's mother became empty [fari'an]﴾ [al-Qasas: 10], meaning empty of everything except anxiety for Musa. It was also said that there is an implied word in the speech, meaning "possessing emptiness and void."

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an) on Surah 14, verse 44:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And warn mankind﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He meant the people of Makkah."

(on the day the punishment comes to them): this is the Day of Resurrection, meaning: warn them of that day. He singled them out with the day of punishment, although it is also the day of reward, because the speech came in the form of a threat to the disobedient.

(Then those who did wrong will say): that is, on that day. (Our Lord, delay us): that is, give us respite.

(for a short term): they asked Him to return them to the worldly life when the truth became manifest in the Hereafter.

(We will answer Your call): that is, to Islam. (And follow the messengers). Then they will be answered: (Did you not swear before [that] there would be no passing away?). That is, in the worldly life. Mujahid said: it is the oath of the Quraysh that they would not be resurrected. Ibn Jurayj said: it is what He related about them in His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [an-Nahl: 38]. (You have no cessation): this has two interpretations. The first: you have no transition from the world to the Hereafter, that is, you will not be resurrected or gathered. This is the view of Mujahid. The second: (You have no cessation) means no cessation from the punishment.

Al-Bayhaqi related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "The people of the Fire have five supplications. Allah answers them in four. When it comes to the fifth, they will never speak again after it. They say: ﴿Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice, so we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way to get out?﴾ [Ghafir: 11]. Then Allah answers them: ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved; but when others were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [Ghafir: 12]."

Then they say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us; we will act righteously; indeed, we are certain﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12]. Then Allah, may He be exalted, answers them: ﴿So taste [the punishment] for having forgotten the meeting of this your Day. Indeed, We have forgotten you, so taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah: 14]. Then they say: "Our Lord, delay us to a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Then Allah, may He be exalted, answers them: "Did you not swear before [that] there would be no passing away?" They say: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will act righteously, not as we used to act﴾ [Fatir: 37]. Then Allah, may He be exalted, answers them: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would be mindful to be mindful? And the warner came to you. So taste [the punishment], for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ [Fatir: 37]. And they say: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 106]. Then Allah answers them: ﴿Be driven away into it, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]. After that they will never speak again. Ibn al-Mubarak recorded it in his "Daqa'iq" in a longer form than this, and we have written it in the book "al-Tadhkirah."

He added in the hadith: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the examples. And they have plotted their plot, but with Allah is their plot, even though their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾ [Ibrahim: 45–46]. He said: "This is the third," and he mentioned the hadith and added, after His saying ﴿Be driven away into it, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]: "Then supplication and hope cease at that point. Some of them turn upon others, attacking one another's faces, and [the punishment] envelops them."

He said: Al-Azhar ibn Abi al-Azhar told me that it was mentioned to him that this refers to His saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35–36].

He said, ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth examples for you﴾. That is, in the lands of Thamud and similar peoples. So why did you not take warning from their dwellings, after what We did to them had become clear to you, and after We had set forth examples for you in the Qur'an? Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read "wa-nubayyin lakum" with a nun and with the jazm (apocopate), treating it as the imperfect with the meaning of the past, so as to match His words "how We dealt with them." The recitation of the majority is "wa-tabayyan," which has the same meaning, because that would not become clear to them except through God's making it clear to them.

He said, ﴿And they had plotted their plot﴾, that is, by associating others with God, denying the messengers, and obstinacy. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas and others.

﴿And with God is their plotting, though their plotting was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾. Here "in" (إن) means "ma," that is, their plotting was not such that the mountains would be moved by it, due to its weakness and feebleness. The particle "in" in the sense of "ma" occurs in the Qur'an in five places. The first is this one. The second is ﴿And if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down to you﴾ [Yunus: 94]. The third is ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were doing [it]﴾ [al-Anbiya': 17], meaning "if We were not doing it." The fourth is ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 81]. The fifth is ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26].

The majority read "wa-in kana" with a nun. 'Amr ibn 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy read "wa-in kada" with a dal. The common reading has a kasra on the lam in "li-tazula," treating it as the lam of denial (lam al-juhud), and a fatha on the second lam, in the accusative. Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Juraij and al-Kisa'i read "li-tazula" with a fatha on the first lam, treating it as the lam of emphasis (lam al-ibtida'), and a raf' (nominative) on the second, with "wa-in" being the light form of the heavy (mukhaffafa min al-thaqila). The meaning of this reading is to magnify their plotting: that is, their plotting was so great that the mountains almost moved from it. Al-Tabari said: the preferred reading is the first, because if they had moved, they would not have remained firm.

Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: there is no proof against the codex of the Muslims in the hadith which Ahmad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Danil [[This chain appears in all the manuscripts, and we have not been able to trace it despite searching.]], who said: I heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: A tyrant among the tyrants said, "I will not stop until I know who is in the heavens." So he took the young of eagles and ordered that they be fed meat until they grew strong and robust and became overgrown [[istaʿjalat: became coarse/gross (ghulliṭat).]]. He ordered that a chest be made large enough for two men, and that a staff be placed in it with a piece of meat of a deep red color fixed to its top. He ordered that the eagles' feet be secured with stakes and tied to the legs of the chest. Then he sat, he and a companion, inside the chest and stirred up the eagles. When they saw the meat, they pursued it, and they kept raising the chest until they reached what Allah willed. The tyrant said to his companion, "Open the door and look, what do you see?" He said, "I see the mountains like flies." He said, "Close the door." Then they ascended with the chest as far as Allah willed. The tyrant said to his companion, "Open the door and look, what do you see?" He said, "I see nothing but the sky, and we only grow farther from it." He said, "Lower the staff," and he lowered it, and the eagles swooped down. When the chest fell to the ground, a crash was heard from it, and the mountains almost moved from their places because of it. He said: I then heard 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, read "wa-in kana makruhum latazulu" with a fatha on the first lam of "latazulu" and a damma on the second.

al-Tha'labi has related this report with the same meaning, and he said that the tyrant was Nimrod, who disputed with Abraham about his Lord. 'Ikrima said: a beardless youth was with him in the chest, who carried a bow and arrows, and he shot them, and they came back to him smeared with blood, and he said, "You have relieved yourself of the God of heaven" [[The wording of al-Tha'labi in "Qisas al-Anbiya'": "You have relieved yourself of the trouble of the God of heaven."]]. 'Ikrima said: it was smeared with the blood of a fish from the sky, which threw itself to him from a sea suspended in the air. It was also said: it was a bird among the birds that the arrow struck. Then Nimrod ordered his companion to strike the staff and to lower the meat, so the eagles descended with the chest. The mountains heard the rustling of the chest and the eagles and were terrified, and they thought that some event had befallen them from the sky, and that the Hour had come. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and though their plotting was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾.

al-Qushayri said: this is possible through the creation of life in the mountains.

al-Mawardi mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that Nimrod ibn Kan'an built the tower (al-sarh) in the town of al-Rass in the outskirts of Kufa. Its height was five thousand and fifty cubits, and its width was three thousand and twenty-five cubits. He ascended it with the eagles. When he realized that there was no way for him to reach the heavens, he made it a fortress and gathered his family and children in it to protect themselves. So Allah brought down its structure from its foundations, and the tower collapsed on them, and they all perished. This is the meaning of ﴿and they had plotted their plot﴾.

Regarding the mountains whose removal their plotting was meant to bring about, there are two views: the first is the mountains of the earth; the second is Islam and the Qur'an, because of their firmness and steadfastness like mountains.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not think that Allah is one who breaks His promise to His messengers﴾. **Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 14, verses 48–52:**

God's words: ﴿On the day the earth is changed to a different earth﴾. That is, mention the day the earth is changed, so the phrase is connected to what precedes it. It was also said that it is a description of His words: ﴿the day the reckoning is established﴾ [Ibrahim: 41]. Scholars differed on how the earth will be changed. Many people said that the change of the earth means a change in its attributes: leveling its hills, flattening its mountains, and stretching its surface. Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated this. Ibn Majah recorded it in his Sunan, and Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it from the hadith of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ibn Abbas told me, "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide and its width will be increased by such and such," and he mentioned the hadith. It was also narrated as a marfu' hadith (traced directly to the Prophet) from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth will be changed into another earth. He will spread it out and stretch it like a leather hide of 'Ukaz [[Adim 'ukazi: attributed to 'Ukaz, a type of leather that was brought there and sold there. 'Ukaz: the name of one of the famous markets of the Jahiliyyah, located near Makkah. Al-Amt: the high ground, small hills, and lowlands and highlands.]] in which there is no crookedness or elevation. Then Allah will drive the creation with one shout, and they will be in the second life in the same places they were in the first: whoever was in its belly will be in its belly, and whoever was on its surface will be on its surface [[The original text here is incomplete and distorted; the addition and correction are taken from Tafsir al-Tabari and the author's book "al-Tadhkirah."]]." This was recorded by al-Ghaznawi.

The change of the heaven means the folding up of its sun and moon and the scattering of its stars, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said that it means the variation of its conditions: at one time it is like molten metal [[See vol. 18, p. 284.]] and at another like red oil [[See vol. 17, p. 173.]]. Ibn al-Anbari related this. We have already explained this subject in detail in the book "al-Tadhkirah," and we mentioned what the scholars said about it, and that the correct view is the removal of this earth, as established from the Prophet (ﷺ). Muslim narrated from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "I was standing before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a rabbi (ḥabr) from among the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said, 'Peace be upon you,'" and he mentioned the hadith. In it, the Jew said: "Where will people be on the day the earth is changed into another earth and the heavens?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In the darkness, before the bridge [[Al-Jisr: the Sirat.]]." And he mentioned the hadith.

It was also recorded from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about His words: "On the day the earth is changed into another earth and the heavens," so where will people be on that day? He said: "On the Sirat." Ibn Majah recorded it with the same chain as Muslim. Al-Tirmidhi also recorded it from Aisha, and she was the one who asked. He said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." These hadiths state explicitly that the heavens and the earth will be changed and removed, and Allah will create another earth on which people will be after being on the bridge.

In Sahih Muslim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white earth, pure, like a loaf of fine wheat flour [[Al-Naqi: the fine sifted flour. Al-Hawwari: that which has been whitened. Al-'Alam: the mark.]], in which there is no mark belonging to anyone."

Jabir said: I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "On the day the earth is changed into another earth." He said: "It will be changed into a loaf of bread from which the creation will eat on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: "And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food [[See vol. 11, p. 272.]]."

Ibn Mas'ud said: It will be changed into another earth, white, on which no sin has been committed. Ibn Abbas said: into an earth of silver, white. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: On that day the earth will be changed to silver and the heaven to gold. This is a change of substance, and that is enough for you.

(And they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer) That is, from their graves, as already mentioned.

God's words: ﴿And you will see the criminals﴾, and they are the polytheists.

(On that day) That is, the Day of Resurrection.

(Bound together) That is, tied up (in chains). (Shackled) These are the shackles and fetters; the singular is ṣafd and ṣafad. It is said: "I shackled him (ṣafadtuhu ṣafdan)," that is, I fettered him, and the noun is al-ṣafad. If you want to intensify it, you say: "I thoroughly shackled him (ṣaffadtuhu taṣfidan)." 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"They returned with plunder and captives,
and we returned with kings shackled [muṣaffadīn]."

That is, bound. Hassan said:

"From every captive whose shackles are tightened,
a falcon when he meets the hated, a protector."

That is, his fetter. "Asfadtuhu ișfādan" means I gave him. It was also said that "ṣafadtuhu" and "asfadtuhu" are both used in the sense of binding and giving. Al-Nabigha said:

"I did not reject—may you never be cursed—the gift [al-ṣafad]."

Al-Ṣufd is the gift, because it binds and enslaves. Abu al-Tayyib said:

"I bound myself in your shelter out of love,
and whoever finds kindness is bound by it."

It was said: each disbeliever will be coupled with a devil in a single shackle. Its explanation is His words: "Gather those who did wrong and their spouses [[See vol. 25, p. 72.]]," meaning their companions among the devils. It was also said that the disbelievers will be gathered in the shackles just as they were gathered in this world in acts of disobedience.

(Their garments of tar) That is, their shirts. According to Ibn Duraid and others, the singular is sirbal, and the verb is tasarbaltu and sarbaltu ghayri. Ka'b ibn Malik said:

"A band of men around the Prophet confronts you,
for them are coats of mail woven by Dawud in battle."

"Of tar": this means the camel tar with which camels are treated for mange, as al-Hasan said. This is more effective in kindling the fire upon them. In the Sahih it is stated that a wailing woman who did not repent before her death will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies. It was narrated from Hammad that they said: it is copper. Isa ibn Umar recited "qaṭrān" with a fatha on the qaf and sukun on the ta'. There is a third reading: kasr of the qaf and jazm of the ta', and from it is the verse of Abu al-Najm:

"A black one, as if the sweat which had oozed out [nataḥa al-'araq: came out of the skin]
clothed him in tar and coarse wool."

A fourth reading, "min qaṭrānin," was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ya'qub. Al-qiṭr is copper and molten brass, and from it is the verse: "Bring me, I will pour over it molten brass [qiṭran]" [[See vol. 11, p. 62.]]. Al-ān is that which has reached its heat, and from it is the verse: "Between a boiling hot water [ḥamīm āin]" [[See vol. 17, p. 175.]].

(And the fire will cover) That is, strike (their faces), so that it covers them.

(That Allah may recompense every soul for what it earned) That is, for what it acquired.

(Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning) Already mentioned.

God's words: ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾. That is, this which We have sent down to you is a message, meaning a conveyance and an admonition.

(And that they may be warned by it) That is, that they may be made to fear the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was read "wa-liyanẓarū" with a fatḥa on the ya' and dhāl. It is said: "naẓirtu bi-l-shay' anẓaru," when one knows of a thing and prepares for it. They did not use a verbal noun from it, just as they did not use one from 'asā and laysa. It seems they were content with "an" and the verb, as in your saying: "sarrani an naẓirtu bi-l-shay'," meaning "it pleased me that I was informed of the thing."

(And that they may know that He is but one God) That is, that they may know the oneness of Allah through the proofs and evidences He has established.

(And that people of understanding may take heed) That is, that people of intellect may be admonished. These lām particles in "wa-liyundharū," "wa-liya'lamū," and "wa-liyadhdhakkara" are connected to an omitted element, and the estimated meaning is: "And for that reason We sent it down." Yaman ibn Ri'ab narrated that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Someone asked some people: "Does the Book of Allah have a title?" He said: "Yes." It was asked: "Where is it?" He said: His words, Exalted is He: "This is a message for mankind, and that they may be warned by it," to the end of the verse.

The commentary on Surat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is complete, and praise belongs to Allah.

Its editor: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim Itfish.

The ninth part of the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi is complete, followed, God willing, by the tenth part, which begins with Surat al-Hijr.

Al-qiṭr is copper and molten brass, and from it is the verse: "Bring me, I will pour over it molten brass [qiṭran]" [[See vol. 11, p. 62.]]. Al-ān is that which has reached its heat, and from it is the verse: "Between a boiling hot water [ḥamīm āin]" [[See vol. 17, p. 175.]].

(And the fire will cover) That is, strike (their faces), so that it covers them.

(That Allah may recompense every soul for what it earned) That is, for what it acquired.

(Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning) Already mentioned.

God's words: ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾. That is, this which We have sent down to you is a message, meaning a conveyance and an admonition.

(And that they may be warned by it) That is, that they may be made to fear the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was read "wa-liyanẓarū" with a fatḥa on the ya' and dhāl. It is said: "naẓirtu bi-l-shay' anẓaru," when one knows of a thing and prepares for it. They did not use a verbal noun from it, just as they did not use one from 'asā and laysa. It seems they were content with "an" and the verb, as in your saying: "sarrani an naẓirtu bi-l-shay'," meaning "it pleased me that I was informed of the thing."

(And that they may know that He is but one God) That is, that they may know the oneness of Allah through the proofs and evidences He has established.

(And that people of understanding may take heed) That is, that people of intellect may be admonished. These lām particles in "wa-liyundharū," "wa-liya'lamū," and "wa-liyadhdhakkara" are connected to an omitted element, and the estimated meaning is: "And for that reason We sent it down." Yaman ibn Ri'ab narrated that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). Someone asked some people: "Does the Book of Allah have a title?" He said: "Yes." It was asked: "Where is it?" He said: His words, Exalted is He: "This is a message for mankind, and that they may be warned by it," to the end of the verse.

The commentary on Surat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is complete, and praise belongs to Allah.

Its editor: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim Itfish.
